title: Biological Hierarchy, the Central Dogma, and the Nucleus
summary: Start with the biological hierarchy, the central dogma, and the idea that every transcriptomic measurement begins as a molecule in a cell.
outcomes: By the end of this capsule a student can
Place the transcriptome on the ladder from organism to molecule,
State the central dogma and its exceptions,
Explain why a gene produces several transcripts,
Justify why transcriptomic data are counts spanning five orders of magnitude, and
Name three biological questions that transcriptomics alone cannot answer
topics: What a gene actually looks like

title: The Anatomy of a Cell: Where mRNA Lives, and Why Sampling Destroys
summary: A focused 20-minute bridge from biological context to the data structures and decisions used in AI for transcriptomics.
outcomes: A student finishing this capsule can
say where in the cell each RNA species is found and what that implies for single\-cell versus single\-nucleus protocols,
describe the extraction chain from tissue to purified RNA,
explain dissociation bias and cell\-composition confounding in their own words, and
interpret RIN, mitochondrial fraction, and 3' bias as quality signals in a public dataset
topics: A guided tour of the cell

title: From Biology to Digital Counts
summary: A focused 20-minute bridge from biological context to the data structures and decisions used in AI for transcriptomics.
outcomes: A student finishing this capsule can
Narrate the path from a lysed cell to a FASTQ file,
Contrast bulk, single\-cell and spatial transcriptomics in terms of what each averages away,
Explain what a UMI corrects and what it does not,
Give the three possible meanings of a zero in a count matrix, and
Diagnose a confounded experimental design from a metadata table
topics: What a sequencer actually gives you

title: Dimensionality Reduction and Visualisation: The Bridge to AI
summary: Close the block by connecting count matrices to PCA, UMAP, autoencoders, and count-aware representation learning.
outcomes: A student finishing this capsule can
justify normalisation and feature selection before any projection,
explain PCA as an SVD and read a scree plot,
use a PCA coloured by covariate as a design diagnostic,
state precisely what a UMAP does and does not preserve, and
situate autoencoders and scVI as non\-linear successors to PCA with a count\-appropriate likelihood
